subject.title: fix: preserve embedded prompt caching across room events and native Responses

question: Should denied room-event, non-owner, and unknown-sender turns retain model-visible schemas for the protected `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` tools when a hard runtime wrapper blocks execution?
rationale: The reviewed implementation is fail-closed and prevents hooks and implementations on denied calls, but the capability-disclosure tradeoff is a permanent security and product boundary that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve stable schemas with hard denial
options.body: Port the design to current main and require exact-head proof that denied calls cannot reach hooks or implementations.

options.title: Keep protected schemas hidden
options.body: Preserve the current disclosure boundary and pursue cache continuity through a different prompt or session architecture.

options.title: Split the protected-tool redesign
options.body: Land delivery and native continuation fixes separately while deferring the schema-visibility policy.

recommendation.title: Approve stable schemas with hard denial
recommendation.body: Port the design to current main and require exact-head proof that denied calls cannot reach hooks or implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest current-main work spans every central conflict, authorization, and provider-routing surface involved in this choice.
